$comment: The San Francisco & San Jose Railroad's old line in San Francisco and San Jose (Phase 2b.D). Geometry: trace.json.

properties.name: Seventh St to Harrison St, by Division St
properties.geometry_method: Traced by eye from USGS San Francisco North 1:24,000 (1950) (10 hand-read points); then traced by eye from USGS San Francisco North 1:24,000 (1950) (9 hand-read points).

sources.note: The 1899 sheet (surveyed 1894) draws the line from Seventh St by Division St, south through the Mission and diagonally to the Bernal Cut.

properties.notes: The old line left the Seventh St tracks at about 16th St and ran west by Division St. The 1950 sheet still draws the track, as a spur, so it is traced from there.

properties.name: The Mission, from 16th St to 26th St
properties.geometry_method: Traced by eye from USGS San Francisco 1:62,500 (1899) (5 hand-read points); then traced by eye from USGS San Francisco 1:62,500 (1899) (8 hand-read points); the sheet corrected by a shift on 3 control points (the same railroad near Division St, where the 1950 San Francisco North sheet still draws it; +115 m E, +220 m N, RMS 0.0 m).

sources.note: The 1899 sheet (surveyed 1894) draws the line from Seventh St by Division St, south through the Mission and diagonally to the Bernal Cut.
The fit's control points: the same railroad near Division St, where the 1950 sheet still draws it.

properties.notes: Traced from the 1899 sheet, which is drawn about 115 m east and 220 m north of where it should be here; the fit moves it back by matching the curve near Division St that both sheets draw.

controls.label: the railroad near Division St, point 1
the railroad near Division St, point 2
the railroad near Division St, point 3

properties.name: 26th St to San Jose Ave

sources.note: The 1899 sheet (surveyed 1894) draws the line from Seventh St by Division St, south through the Mission and diagonally to the Bernal Cut.

properties.notes: The 1899 sheet ends at 37°45′ N, partway along this stretch, and the 1915 sheet south of it draws the city too densely to read the railroad. Drawn straight on, at the 1899 sheet's bearing, to San Jose Ave, so it is approximate.

properties.name: The Bernal Cut, along San Jose Ave
properties.geometry_method: Along today's San Jose Avenue centerline from -122.42233,37.74719 to -122.43342,37.73279 (2168 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1, across gaps of up to 60 m where the street is cut today); checked on USGS San Francisco South 1:24,000 (1950).

sources.note: The 1950 sheet draws San Jose Ave in the cut, with the railroad's label beside it.

properties.notes: San Jose Ave and BART took over the cut; the railroad is drawn on today's San Jose Ave centerline, within about 30 m of the track.

properties.name: Glen Park to San Bruno, by Ocean View and Colma
properties.geometry_method: Traced by eye from USGS San Francisco South 1:24,000 (1950) (8 hand-read points); then traced by eye from USGS San Francisco South 1:24,000 (1950) (21 hand-read points); then traced by eye from USGS San Francisco South 1:24,000 (1950) (9 hand-read points); then traced by eye from USGS San Francisco South 1:24,000 (1950) (14 hand-read points); then traced by eye from USGS San Francisco South 1:24,000 (1950) (16 hand-read points); then traced by eye from USGS San Francisco South 1:24,000 (1950) (16 hand-read points); then traced by eye from USGS San Francisco South 1:24,000 (1950) (5 hand-read points); then traced by eye from USGS San Francisco South 1:24,000 (1950) (13 hand-read points).

sources.note: The 1950 sheet still draws the line as the Southern Pacific's, from Glen Park to San Bruno.

properties.notes: BART runs beside or on much of this right-of-way today. Traced from the 1950 sheet, where the track still ran.

properties.name: San José: the old main line to the Market Street station
properties.geometry_method: Traced by eye from USGS San Jose 1:62,500 (1943) (11 hand-read points).

sources.note: The main line "enters the City from the northwest near the end of Autumn Street, runs eastward across San Pedro, North First, North Second and North Third streets and then turns southerly and follows Fourth Street" (OCR).
The new line of 1935 "leaves the old line at Polhemus Street".

properties.notes: From the junction at Polhemus Street east through the station yard, as the 1943 sheet still draws it, to the yard's east end near Fourth St. The line ran on down Fourth St to Reed St and south to Lick; that part isn't drawn yet.

properties.name: The Los Altos branch, Mayfield by Los Altos and Monta Vista to Vasona Junction

sources.note: The first timetable with the cut-off, effective April 19, 1908.
"It is double-track as far as Congress Junction."
From 1910 the west track to Congress Junction was given to the Peninsular Railway's electric cars.

properties.notes: Built by the Southern Pacific's Peninsular Railroad (the Mayfield cut-off); double track to Congress Junction, the west track used by the Peninsular Railway's electric cars from 1910, which aren't drawn yet. Much of the right of way is the Foothill Expressway today (Campbell Press, 1963).
properties.geometry_method: OpenHistoricalMap ways 198540837, 199596214, 199596213, 198748393 (CC0, as of 2026-10-16), which OHM's mappers drew from https://www.santacruztrains.com/2021/10/streetcars-peninsular-railway-company.html; checked on USGS Palo Alto 1:24,000 (1953), USGS San Jose West 1:24,000 (1953) and USGS Los Gatos 1:62,500 (1919). OpenHistoricalMap's ways from the Peninsula main line at Mayfield (California Ave) by Los Altos, Loyola, Monta Vista and Congress Junction to Vasona Junction on the South Pacific Coast's line.
